claims.text: Lockheed's Advanced Development Projects designed and flew the U-2, A-12/SR-71 and F-117 under security regimes in which the aircraft's existence was officially denied while operational.

CIA's own historical account confirms that U-2 and OXCART overflights were the source of a majority of UFO reports in the late 1950s and 1960s, and that false explanations were issued to protect them.
Lockheed Martin was publicly challenged in March 2023 over allegations concerning UFO legacy programmes, in named-source reporting.

desc: Advanced projects organisations are the industrial layer at which secrecy and engineering are the same activity. Lockheed's Skunk Works is the documented archetype: a walled-off division with its own security, its own contracting relationship, and a demonstrated ability to design, build and fly aircraft - U-2, A-12, F-117 - that the government publicly denied existed while they were flying. Ben Rich's own memoir describes that regime from the inside. The reason this domain matters to the board is that the same organisations are the only plausible industrial home for an exploitation programme: they hold the facility clearances, the special access programme infrastructure, the machinists and metallurgists, and the independent research and development accounts through which company money can be spent without a government line item. The dual-use route is therefore not a route at all - the capability is identical, and only the input differs. Northrop Grumman, Lockheed Martin, Raytheon and Battelle Memorial Institute recur across witness accounts precisely because they are the entities that could do it. Scoring high on this domain means an entity is one of those organisations or worked at that level inside one.
